articles.title: I Just Found Out Sylvester Stallone Caused Some DRAMA After I Play Rocky Got Announced
articles.summary: A little misunderstanding led to a BIG issue.
articles.content:
Rocky has returned to the big screen amid the 2026 movie schedule , but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected. Sylvester Stallone ’s journey to getting the iconic 1976 film made is chronicled in the acclaimed biopic, I Play Rocky , which is helmed by Peter Farrelly. While Stallone had no direct involvement in the movie, he did give it his official stamp of approval to the creative team. However, the beloved actor accidentally sparked some serious drama after the movie was announced, and I was totally unaware of it.

Honestly, the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s rationale (as shared on X ) makes a lot of sense. If Stallone were credited as a producer on the film, which shows him in a mostly positive light, many may be tempted to think he manipulated the narrative. The Rambo star is, of course, no stranger to moviemaking so, given his directing and producing experience, I can see why he’d agree. Despite coming to an accord on Stallone needing to “separate” himself from the production, that apparently led to a serious faux pas on the actor’s part:

The mere thought of getting heat from fans is daunting enough, but receiving heat from a member of the Stallone family is something else entirely. Farrelly went on to say that he later had another chat with the purveyor and lover of the Rocky films , and it went down as follows:

While all this drama was due to a simple misunderstanding, it definitely created quite a mess for the filmmaking team. No lasting damage was seemingly done, though, and I’d say that things have been working out for Farrelly and his collaborators. The movie has been well received and gaining considerable buzz in the lead-up to the Oscars. It even received a stamp of approval from Ryan Gosling . As for Stallone, he admitted he was prepared to be “hypercritical” of the film, but he ended up really enjoying the movie as a whole and lead actor Anthony Ippolito’s portrayal of him.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! Ever since the One Piece manga began serialization in 1997, Luffy has steadily grown more powerful. His journey has brought him several challenges, and there's no denying he grew more powerful each time he overcame an obstacle. Of course, there were times like the Sabaody Archipelago and the Marineford Arc where he just couldn't win, no matter how hard he tried. However, even those experiences shaped him to be the person he is today. Throughout the years, he transforms from a no-name rookie pirate into one of the Four Emperors of the Sea. This only happened because of his Gear 5 transformation, something he was only able to achieve after his Devil Fruit awakening.

It's easily one of the best-written Shonen transformations of all time since it not only gives Luffy a huge power-up, but it also has centuries and maybe even millennia of history behind it. There's no doubt Luffy is now one of the most powerful characters in the series, and he can easily take down almost everyone who crosses his path. However, because of his drawback, he is unable to make full use of his abilities. Now that the manga is in its Elbaph Arc, he is undergoing another mysterious transformation that could mean a huge power-up. However, as of now, it's unlikely he will be able to defeat these five characters.

Even as one of the most important characters in the series, much about  Blackbeard is still a mystery . While the Elbaph Arc delved into his origins, his powers haven't been fully revealed yet. The series has yet to explain the reason he is able to possess the power of two Devil Fruits. Not only does he have two unimaginably powerful Devil Fruits at his disposal, but he is also an exceptionally skilled Haki user. Blackbeard is not only strong but also crafty, who would resort to any means necessary to accomplish his goals.

He is also someone Shanks considers a major threat, which makes him all the more dangerous. There's still no guarantee which of the two is stronger in terms of raw power, but it's evident that if they were to fight, Luffy would have a huge disadvantage at his current level. This is simply because his chances of winning would be considerably slim if he runs out of stamina and needs a break to eat food and replenish his energy.

Loki was introduced in the Elbaph Arc , and the series didn't waste any time before confirming he is already a top-tier character. As Harald's son who has the blood of the Ancient Giants running through his veins, Loki was already multiple times stronger than any average Giant. However, thanks to the legendary Devil Fruit and Ragnir, Loki is on a completely different level. His Devil Fruit allows the user to transform into the largest dragon in the world, but the size depends on the one who consumes it.

This is why the fruit’s true potential can only be achieved by an ancient Giant like Loki who was chosen by Ragnir to possess the power of this fruit. The ancient legend describes the mythical dragon as a being so vast that it envelops the sky with darkness and breathes lightning. As the fight continues in the manga, Loki even fought Imu one-on-one, something not everyone is capable of. It turned out well that Loki is actually an ally of Luffy, since he needs more powerful fighters on his side in the long run.

Mihawk is another one of those characters who mostly remains a mystery even after almost 30 years since the story began. Even though the true extent of his powers is unknown and he has absolutely no feats to speak of, his title alone is enough for him to rank in this list. Mihawk is not only the first Warlord introduced in the story, but he is someone Zoro must surpass before he can become the world's strongest swordsman.

From his sword skills to how powerful his Haki is, fans have long been curious about everything related to this character. He and Shanks used to be rivals, and they were considered equals in power. Even the Final Saga has yet to shed more light on the character and his abilities. There hasn't been any opportunity for him to showcase his true power, but that might change in the Final War that will envelop the entire world in flames.

Shanks is not only one of the most crucial characters in the story, but  his powers are overwhelming , even against characters like the Admirals and other Emperors of the Sea. He is Luffy’s role model who spent one year in his village and helped him set out on the path to becoming a pirate. Shanks is not only a swordsman, but his Haki is second to none. No other character has demonstrated a more powerful Conqueror's Haki than he did at the end of the Wano Country Saga, where he intimidated Admiral Green Bull from miles away.

Fans have always known how powerful he is, but after that display, it really raises the question if any other character other than Imu can best him in raw power. While Luffy’s Haki and abilities aren’t something to scoff at, the young pirate hasn’t displayed a power strong enough to overwhelm Shanks, who earned his nickname of Haki Killer since he is the only character known to temporarily block someone's future sight.

Imu finally made his true debut in the Elbaph Arc , and he is more powerful than fans realize. While there have been debates about the final antagonist before, his feats in the Elbaph Arc leave no room for doubt that Imu is the greatest obstacle standing in Luffy's way. Luffy used his Gear 5 abilities in the Elbaph Arc, and the villain effortlessly defeated the young pirate. Having seen Joyboy's true powers, Imu knows better than anyone that Luffy is nowhere near as powerful as he should be.

Aside from his immortality, what truly makes Imu terrifying is his demonic powers and the weapons he possesses from the First Twenty, the rulers of the Allied Nations during the time of the World Government's establishment. Imu is by no means an ordinary fighter, since his powers are akin to a mythical God or maybe a demon. Since the fight in Elbaph is still ongoing, there's always a chance we might see more of this villain's true powers.

Which of these  One Piece  characters do you think poses the biggest challenge for Luffy? Is there anyone else he cannot defeat at his current level? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Why Did the Hunger Games Cut Major McKenna Grace Scenes? Sunrise on the Reaping Director Addresses the Backlash
articles.summary: While most viewers are loving the newest entry in the Hunger Games franchise (it's holding tight to its 94% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes), it seems Francis Lawrence, the film's director, is in hot water with book fans and has had to take to the internet to try to clear up a few points about […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While most viewers are loving the newest entry in the Hunger Games franchise (it's holding tight to its 94% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes), it seems Francis Lawrence, the film's director, is in hot water with book fans and has had to take to the internet to try to clear up a few points about choices that were made when it came to the film's final cut. What is it that has book fans so upset? The jarring removal of scenes that were central to the book, and especially to the character of Maysilee Donner, one of the tributes who formed an alliance with Haymitch Abernathy.

Speaking with Bustle about these changes and why they were made , Lawrence said simply, "It wasn't doing anything for us in terms of character or thematics at that point in the movie." It feels especially jarring considering how faithful the adaptations of previous books in the series, also directed by Lawrence, have been (we're ignoring that Peeta kept his leg in the movies). And fans really aren't buying the reasoning, claiming that these cut scenes (there was also a scene involving a porcupine mutt that didn't make the final cut, as well as some others) would have added a serious amount of depth, as well as showing the audience more of who these characters were. "So he didn’t read the book," said one fan.

In the book, Haymitch and Donner find themselves face-to-face with three lower-level Gamemakers in the arena, working as janitors and cleaning up the mess left behind after a water tank breaks. The pair kill the janitors, which effectively sets them on their final journey within the games. But this scene didn't make it into the final cut, much to fans' confusion. There was also a scene where Haymitch lures a bear-sized porcupine mutt into a trap, defending himself with a shield and an axe before eventually escaping.

When asked about the scenes, Lawrence noted that even the producers disagreed over whether or not the scenes were even necessary. He said, “That janitor sequence… we shot it, but there was a lot of discussion around it. Initially, when we screened the movie for people, we had that sequence in." He went on to add, “There's probably a five- to 10-minute stretch in there around porcupine, which people might remember, and a little bit of a fight after the janitors. That all got lifted out." The director was quick to note, however, that these scenes might not be lost forever, and instead will find their way to whatever extended edition or deleted scenes make their way to physical media—though he's also been vocal about not wanting the original four hour and 12 minute cut to be available as a director's cut. "I don't want anybody to see the four, 12 minute cut," he told BAFTA.

articles.title: Why Another ‘Hunger Games’ Movie Isn’t Coming Anytime Soon
articles.summary: “The Hunger Games” franchise has caught fire once again. “Sunrise on the Reaping,” the sixth installment in the billion-dollar dystopian franchise, has defied expectations and opened to $120 million at the box office, nearly tripling the $44 million opening of the 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” Surely part of the success here […]
articles.content:
“The Hunger Games” franchise has caught fire once again.

“Sunrise on the Reaping,” the sixth installment in the billion-dollar dystopian franchise, has defied expectations and opened to $120 million at the box office, nearly tripling the $44 million opening of the 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.”

Surely part of the success here is the Jennifer Lawrence factor: The star’s return (alongside Josh Hutcherson) was first reported by Variety nearly a year ago — and the duo’s reunion with fellow franchise veterans Woody Harrelson, Elizabeth Banks and Jena Malone at the film’s New York premiere ignited seismic levels of buzz online . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Anne Hathaway to Receive American Riviera Award at Santa Barbara International Film Festival CAA Signs Horror Creator ThatMob for Representation

According to social media analytics firm RelishMix , ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ amassed a social media reach of 652 million. That doesn’t trail far behind the 680 million pre-opening reach of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” — and represents a staggering 66% jump from “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes’” 393 million (more on par with the pre-opening reach of Disney’s “Hexed” at 391.9 million).

So, in today’s IP-fueled Hollywood landscape, the blazing success of “Sunrise on the Reaping” would light a fire under the asses of most studio execs to get a seventh “Hunger Games” movie on the calendar as swiftly as possible. While it’d be a fool’s bet to call this the definitive end of the franchise on the big screen, the odds of Lionsgate gifting fans another movie announcement this holiday season aren’t exactly in our favor.

The key here is Suzanne Collins , who has maintained an active creative role in the franchise since the film rights to her planned trilogy were acquired for $200,000 in 2009. Collins co-wrote the screenplay for the first film and has remained deeply involved in each film, working closely with franchise director Francis Lawrence on everything from story development to reviewing final cuts. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

After the Jennifer Lawrence-led saga concluded in 2015 with “Mockingjay — Part 2,” the franchise sat dormant until 2020 when Collins published “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” The prequel, set 64 years before Katniss Everdeen entered the arena, explores how an 18-year-old Coriolanus Snow became the tyrannical president of Panem. Lionsgate adapted the novel into a 2023 film and remained in lockstep with Collins, announcing its adaptation of “Sunrise on the Reaping” on June 6, 2024: the same day Scholastic unveiled her latest novel.

At the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere, when the topic of a seventh “Hunger Games” movie came up, everyone from the franchise’s creative forces to Lionsgate’s top brass delivered the same message: We’re waiting on Suzanne.

“She does not do anything in a frivolous fashion,” Lionsgate chairman Adam Fogelson told Variety at the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere. “When she believes she has an important story to tell, I believe she will write it and we will be the beneficiaries of it. But nothing I can say or do — nothing anyone could say or do — is going to shake her core fundamental desire to be inspired to write a great story.” Collins attended the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere, joining a behemoth group photo that brought together Lawrence and the vets who worked on the original four films, Rachel Zegler and the “Songbirds and Snakes” crew and the fresh crop of tributes from the latest installment.

The press-shy author didn’t give any interviews, but while signing autographs for fans, she offered an ambiguous two words when asked whether another novel was on the way: “We’ll see.” (Fans on X were considerably less restrained, with one parody account declaring : “SUZANNE COLLINS CONFIRMED A NEW HUNGER GAMES BOOK”).

Perhaps the fans are right, and this is all one big game of Werewulf, but Lawrence insists that he hasn’t caught so much as a whiff of another book.

“I’m telling you — the studio doesn't believe us, I don’t think anybody believes us — but she does not tell us a word,” Lawrence explained. “She gives us no hints if she’s writing or not.” The director added that he doesn’t think the studio is necessarily “comfortable” with the prolonged waits between Collins’ novels: “I think they wish that she’d just be pumping them out. But, you know, she does her thing. And that’s part of what makes them so great.”

Whichever direction the franchise heads next, the numbers suggest there are limits to its appeal — and that not every trip to Panem is guaranteed to draw the same crowd. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Haymitch Abernathy’s origin story has struck a significantly stronger chord with the fanbase than President Snow’s, both on the page and on screen. “Sunrise on the Reaping” sold more than 1.2 million U.S. copies in its first week, twice the first-week sales of “Songbirds and Snakes” and three times those of “Mockingjay.” By January 2026, worldwide English-language sales had surpassed 4.4 million copies.

That success translated to the big screen: “Sunrise on the Reaping” currently holds the highest audience score on Rotten Tomatoes (94%) and Letterboxd rating (4.1/5) in the franchise, even surpassing the beloved “Catching Fire” ( 89% audience RT score ; 4.0/5 Letterboxd ).

Hollywood has also seen the pitfalls of stretching a franchise beyond its source material to capitalize on its commercial success. Most infamously, HBO forged ahead on a final season of “Game of Thrones” as George R.R. Martin struggled to complete his sixth “A Song of Ice and Fire” novel, culminating in a wildly divisive final season that prompted more than a million fans to petition for a remake . Martin later revealed in 2022 that he had been largely “out of the loop” during the show’s final seasons.

“If you look at our relationship with Stephenie [Meyer] on ‘Twilight,’ Chad [Stahelski] and Keanu [Reeves] on ‘John Wick,’ or our longstanding relationship with the ‘Saw’ creators, this is a studio that has prided itself on making great content, but never underestimated how important it is that the architects of that creation continue to have a voice in the process,” Fogelson said, reaffirming Collins as “the creative architect” of the “Hunger Games” franchise. “We have made sure that she is a true partner with our studio across the board. And I think the movies, the campaigns, and everything we do are better for it.

“ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ” is playing in theaters now.

articles.title: Robert Eggers Says He's "Eager" to Take a Break From Horror Genre After 'Werwulf'
articles.summary: The filmmaker has focused on horror films in recent years, including 'The Witch,' 'The Lighthouse,' 'Nosferatu' and 'Werwulf.'
articles.content:
After more than five years of bringing monsters to life on screen, Robert Eggers admits he needs a break from the horror genre.

During a recent Q&A in Mexico, the filmmaker said , "I’m eager not to continue purposely doing Robert Eggers’ House of Horror."

His comments come ahead of the release of Werwulf on Christmas Day. The film, starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Lily-Rose Depp and Willem Dafoe, is set in 14th-century England and follows a town haunted by a beast that threatens a man (Taylor-Johnson) and his family. Related Stories Movies We Now Know What Robert Pattinson Was Doing When the James Bond Casting News Broke Movies Aaron Taylor-Johnson's Monstrous Transformation Teased in Robert Eggers' 'Werwulf' Trailer

"I don’t need to do The Mummy or The Phantom of the Opera . Not to say that I won’t, but I think I need a break," Eggers added. The director previously tackled witches in 2015's The Witch , sea creatures in 2019's The Lighthouse and vampires in 2024's Nosferatu . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Robert Eggers, who has been praised as a modern icon in horror filmmaking, also addressed the new-wave concept of "elevated horror" within cinema .

"There's always been horror movies that don't suck and there's always been horror movies that are actually probing what darkness is in humankind, and even some of them that have been profound throughout the ages," he explained. "But what you guys are talking about is something that I think really started with [2014's] It Follows . Although Ti West was doing this kind of work before then."

"There's been a whole lot of filmmakers that have wanted to make personal films, really talented filmmakers with unique voices, and have realized that they can get financing if they do it as a genre film," the filmmaker continued. "And I think that that's kind of what this is: people who are telling personal stories with unique voices but are doing it through genre. Not to say that James Wan movies [ Insidious , The Conjuring ] haven't worked. They've been great and also successful. There's definitely a hunger for horror in general over the past 10 years. But does elevated horror exist? It does. It does because people say so." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While enjoying his "break" from horror, Eggers is next taking on an adaptation of William Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet for Focus Features .

He previously shared during a post-screening Q&A at Beyond Fest in September, "I was doing something else. But what happened was, after Werwulf , I was writing another horror movie, and it got so dark again, and I was like, 'I need a break. So, I’ll do something about two teenagers killing themselves.'"

articles.title: I Never Knew Patrick Stewart Called Up Kyle MacLachlan For Advice Before Joining Star Trek
articles.summary: The actor shared a little about their conversation.
articles.content:
The late Patrick Stewart was best known for his work in Star Trek , as he became synonymous with the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. With that, it's funny to think that the beloved star ever had reservations about joining the iconic sci franchise. Now, his friend and actor Kyle MacLachlan is opening up about that apprehension, and I can't believe I never knew Stewart rang him up shortly before he committed to The Next Generation .

Based on those comments, it seemed Patrick Stewart had some concerns about committing to a TV series, which could potentially air for a while and prevent him from taking on other roles as an actor. He probably had a lot on his mind, as MacLachlan said, wondering if the benefit of joining Trek would outweigh the missed opportunities elsewhere.

That tapestry of work will extend to the end of the 2026 movie schedule , as the late Stewart will appear as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday later this year. Stewart reportedly told co-stars backstage that it would be his final acting performance , marking his retirement. Stewart would refute those claims months later, saying that he considered acting to be something he would do his entire life .

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google DC Comics has always had an expansive universe with characters and locations that spark the reader’s imagination. Although DC doesn’t have nearly as many iconic fictional countries as Marvel does, the company has still multiple sovereign nations that are fully original. These countries oftentimes have histories that date back thousands of years. More importantly, these countries are classified as world powers. With their unique resources, advanced technology and magic, vast armies, and populations filled to the brim with powerful superhumans, these countries are practically untouchable. Any foreign country or supervillain would be foolish to try and invade these mighty nations.

Some of the most fantastical areas in DC Comics are countries with all manner of superheroes and sophisticated technology within their borders.

A small nation in the middle of the Yellow Sea off the west coast of North Korea, Oolong Island is a paradise for mad scientists everywhere. Originally a protectorate of China, the island was controlled by the mutant Chinese mad scientist Egg Fu, who sought to make it a haven for criminal scientists where they could flourish and develop weapons of mass destruction. Soon enough, bizarre yet brilliant mad scientists like Dr. Sivanna, T.O. Morrow, Dr. Cyclops, came flooding. Under the orders of the Chinese Government, Oolong Island created weapons capable of destroying the Black Marvel Family and Khandaq. Ultimately, this would lead to a superhuman war that resulted in Oolong Island becoming an official sovereign nation under the control of longtime Wonder Woman villain Veronica Cale. Yet even with its new leadership, Oolong Island continues acting as one of the foremost producers of technological innovations and deadly weaponry thanks to its maniacal populous. 

The newest country on this list, El Caldero was once a small and inconsequential on the world stage until a giant meteorite made of pure Kryptonite crash-landed into it. Under the control of President Castilho, El Caldero harnessed the Kryptonite to become one of the wealthiest and technologically advanced nations on the planet practically overnight. They even have Krypto-Knights and mechas to act as El Caldero’s elite guard. Yet despite being a country that’s literally toxic to Superman, El Caldero and its people have nothing but love and appraisal for the Man of Steel. However, things soon turned bad when General Zod overthrew El Caldero’s leadership and sought to have Earth be overrun with a fast-growing and lethal Kryptonite wave. Thankfully, Superman managed to defeat Zod and get rid of all the Kryptonite that threatened to destroy the world. Even without their Kryptonite, El Caldero remains a prosperous country that still views Superman as their hero.

For over three thousand years, the nation of Kahndaq had a history of hardship until the return of its savior. Resting in the Sinai Peninsula that connects Africa to Asia, Kahndaq was the birthplace of Black Adam. In 1600 BC, Kahndaq was ransacked by Egypt, which led to Black Adam going on a rampage and being imprisoned by the wizard Shazam. In the modern day, Kahndaq was controlled by the cruel dictator Asim Muhunnad until Black Adam was freed from his imprisonment. Black Adam immediately killed Asim and established himself as Kahndaq’s new ruler. Yet despite his violent takeover, Black Adam is beloved by his people who view him as a hero. With his incredible powers alongside the rest of the Black Marvel Family, Black Adam ushered in a prosperous new age for Kahndaq. Yet even after suffering from significant catastrophes, Kahndaq always rises from the ashes. Although in more recent comics Black Adam has stepped down as Kahndaq’s ruler, his loyalty will always be to the prosperity of his people.

Founded thousands of years ago by the Greek Goddesses, Themyscira, or Paradise Island, is the beautiful home of the immortal Amazons and their champion, Wonder Woman. The Amazons were created to being peace and enlightenment to the world , but after being enslaved Hercules and his barbarian army, these warrior women hid themselves away from humanity. Themyscira is a thriving island where the Amazons have become masters of both magic and technology. Additionally, almost their entire population are made up of immortal superhumans who have centuries of combat experience. They constantly trained to prepare for the day that they’d have to defend their borders if they were ever discovered. However, the Amazon’s isolationist philosophy was challenged when pilot Steve Trevor crash-landed on their shores and was rescued by Princess Diana. As Wonder Woman, Diana would not only take Steve back home but become an ambassador for Themyscira. Still, the Amazons are still very wary of outsiders and rarely allow men onto their shores. 

Deep beneath the waves lies the most powerful country in DC Comics: Atlantis. This mighty nation was founded millions of years ago by a subspecies of humans called Homo Magi that were naturally skilled with magic. Overtime Atlantis combined magic and technology to become the most advanced nation on Earth. However, thousands of years ago, the mad king Atlan used his magical scepter to sink the continent-sized country underwater. While many died in the cataclysm, most of the Atlantean people evolved to their new underwater environment. Atlantis would hide from the rest of humanity until the superhero Aquaman took his rightful place on the throne and introduced his kingdom to the surface world. Never losing their advancements in magic and technology, Atlantis has the power to effortlessly submerge most of the world’s landmasses. Thankfully, Atlantis now seeks to form stronger ties with humanity and live in peace under Aquaman’s leadership.

Which of these DC nations would you want to live in? Leave a Comment below and join the conversation in the  ComicBook Forum!

articles.title: Wondered What's Going On With Disney World's Indiana Jones Ride? We Have Our First Look
articles.summary: The Imagineers definitely aren't making this up as they go.
articles.content:
Holiday time at Walt Disney World is always one of the best times to visit, but theme park fans might want to postpone their trips to the “Most Magical Place on Earth” until later in 2027. That's when all the new and upcoming attractions are slated to open , like the new Indiana Jones ride in Animal Kingdom. In case anyone has been wondering, Imagineers have been hard at work on the ride, and they’re finally giving fans a first look at the magic they’re crafting.

Time heals most wounds, though, and now that the sting of losing Dinosaur has started to wane, most fans are finally getting excited for the new attraction. To further build excitement, Walt Disney Imagineering shared the following clip on its Instagram:

I was definitely not thrilled about the Animal Kingdom changes at first, but I think I’m going to love this new version of Indiana Jones! I’m definitely on board with the name that was announced back at D23 earlier this year, and I absolutely love the Mayan-inspired facade. Dare I say it puts the Indiana Jones temple at Disneyland to shame (and hopefully won't have to deal with brawls over line cutting ).

When the ride eventually opens sometime next year, guests will embark on an adventure alongside Indy that will take them to a temple that legend says has a water passageway that leads to an underworld protected by a mythic serpent. Imagineers are still keeping much of the actual ride experience under wraps for now. However, with two other cart-style Indiana Jones attractions at other Disney parks and reports that the Dinosaur ride is being rethemed instead of totally demolished, it’s safe to say that this version of Indiana Jones will take guests on a bumpy ride full of twists, turns, snakes (or serpents in this case), and adventure.

articles.title: One Hunger Games Book Change Bothered Me Back In The Day, But Now I Understand Why It Was Made
articles.summary: I've changed my tune since 2012.
articles.content:
I can’t believe the release of Sunrise on the Reaping means I’ve been going to the theaters for The Hunger Games movies for nearly fifteen years! I’ll never forget when I went to see one of my favorite novels at the time become a book-to-screen adaptation back in 2012. I just rewatched the franchise and recalled one gripe I had about the movie when I first saw it that I actually understand now as an adult.

These days I think the original The Hunger Games movie is pretty great, and I’ve rewatched it so many times. I remember when I went to see it back then, I thought it was a faithful adaptation, but I was bummed that they decided to take out the fact that Peeta loses his leg in The Hunger Games . Check out this excerpt from the end of the first book:

In the movie, Peeta gets injured like in the book, but Katniss nurses him back to health, and he completely recovers by the end. Yet, in the source material, Peeta is practically bleeding out right before they become the final people in the arena. Katniss is desperate to help him, and she suggests they both have poisonous berries so she can save them both. When they reunite for the post-victory interview with Caesar Flickerman, she learns that his leg had to be amputated right after they left the arena.

However, it just dawned on me during my recent rewatch (with my Hulu subscription ) that I haven’t thought about this change to The Hunger Games in a really long time. I guess, ultimately, it didn’t really matter that Peeta only has one leg in the scope of the whole series, and it probably would have caused some extra special effects headaches for the filmmaking team.

articles.title: Would Star Wars’ Most Divisive Director Want to Return? Rian Johnson Addresses Future Interest in the Series
articles.summary: It's no secret that you either love Rian Johnson or you hate him. At least, that's the case if you're a Star Wars fan, and fans have always been vocal about their stance on the director, with The Last Jedi, the second film in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, becoming one of the franchise's most […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It's no secret that you either love Rian Johnson or you hate him. At least, that's the case if you're a Star Wars fan , and fans have always been vocal about their stance on the director, with The Last Jedi , the second film in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, becoming one of the franchise's most divisive films. It's also a well-known fact that Johnson left the franchise on less-than-stellar terms—both in a fandom sense and in his working relationship with Kathleen Kennedy before she stepped down as head honcho . But would the director ever return? Seemingly, the answer is "yes."

This weekend at the Marrakech Film Festival , Johnson touched on all sorts of things, including his feelings about Curry Barker representing hope in the effort to save indie filmmaking . And when he was inevitably asked if he'd return to a galaxy far, far away, Johnson said it was a world he "deeply loved." He had initially jumped at the opportunity to direct a Star Wars film, and elaborated on his experience, saying, “I love Star Wars more now than I ever have. And it’s exciting to me that there are a lot of different voices now, taking cracks at it. I’m already writing the next thing I’m gonna do, and it’s not a Star Wars thing or a Knives Out thing." He added, "Right now, I’m very much enjoying making my own stuff, but if the opportunity presented itself, it’s a world I deeply love.”

"I felt just so connected to it, and just cared so deeply about every single element of it. I think, especially with something that has a big cultural impact and belongs to everybody, that makes it even more important for you and the entire team to make it personal for yourselves, to make sure it’s coming from a personal perspective and something that’s deeply on fire inside of you," he said about his desire to do something special with the second film in the sequel trilogy. And it's undeniable that he took risks, creating something that the franchise had never seen before.

As expected, Star Wars fans are divided, though the most common opinion is to give Johnson his own standalone film and "let him cook," or to set him free in the Old Republic era. "After his film, the studio executives have gone overly cautious. Some potentially fascinating films by amazing filmmakers have been proposed and canned. It's a real shame," said one fan on X, highlighting how Disney has overcorrected in the wake of the disaster that was The Rise of Skywalker , shelving projects like The Hunt for Ben Solo and canceling shows like The Acolyte .

articles.title: Mahershala Ali Says "There Are Not Roles for Me" in "Vast Majority of Projects," Despite Winning 2 Oscars
articles.summary: The actor previously took home Academy Awards for best supporting actor for 2016’s 'Moonlight' and 2018's 'Green Book.'
articles.content:
Mahershala Ali is getting candid about why "there are not roles" for him in "the vast majority of projects," despite having already won two Oscars.

During a recent interview on Carmelo Anthony and Kazeem “Kaz” Famuyide’s 7PM in Brooklyn podcast , the actor — who previously took home Academy Awards for best supporting actor for 2016’s Moonlight and 2018's Green Book — opened up about how earning Hollywood's highest recognition doesn't guarantee access to great roles.

"There's a lot of great actors that don't have Oscars, who are also looking for good material," he said. "And that's no disrespect to The Academy or the award at all, but what I'm actually saying is that Oscar or no Oscar, there's a lot of good actors out there. There's more good actors than there is good material." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Katelin Arizmendi on Bringing a New Perspective to Action With 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' Movies Mahershala Ali Put His Two Oscars Into a Cabinet: "I Felt a Sense of Accomplishment, Not Fulfillment"

"It’s not even that all these people are competing for these same spots. It’s just that out of all the material made, there’s only a handful of them that check certain boxes. And then you got to be right for it," Ali continued. "The vast majority of projects that get greenlit, there are not roles for me in those. You gotta think that way, you know what I mean? So, it doesn’t matter if I got 17 Oscars. If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you’re like everybody else waiting and looking and searching."

Given the current political climate, Ali later added that rollbacks of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) funding and initiatives also "on some level impact what gets greenlit."

"I don't know how much of an impact it has, but I just know that if certain companies are allowed to not feel a pressure to be reflective of the world we live in, they'll just keep centering who they see in their offices, and it ain't a bunch of us in those offices," he said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star explained that the only other option for actors is to produce and create their own projects; however, "that's a five-year journey itself."

Famuyide later asked Ali about the fan notion that Black actors are "validated" only after winning an Oscar. "It’s kind of just talk. It doesn’t translate to anything real," the actor replied.

"You don’t want to find yourself in a situation where, oh, that’s ‘the diversity project.’ You just want to do great material as a Black person. articles.summary: It's always a special treat for fans to see their favorite anime series get revitalized years after the finale airs, whether it be a special pop-up that gives fans the opportunity to pick up new merchandise featuring their favorite characters, or, though rare, a brand-new season that revitalizes the fandom in full force. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It's always a special treat for fans to see their favorite anime series get revitalized years after the finale airs, whether it be a special pop-up that gives fans the opportunity to pick up new merchandise featuring their favorite characters, or, though rare, a brand-new season that revitalizes the fandom in full force. One such series, a cult-classic romance titled Inu x Boku SS , recently celebrated a major milestone and delivered by giving fans a stunning new illustration showcasing all of the main cast in commemorative outfits. The anime adaptation of Cocoa Fujiwara's original manga is officially celebrating its 15th anniversary by revamping the franchise's official website with new artwork from the series' character designer and chief animation director, Haruko Iizuka.

Inu x Boku SS was produced by David Productions, based on the original manga by Cocoa Fujiwara published in Square Enix's Gangan Joker . The series follows a young heiress named Ririchiyo Shirakiin who is fiercely protected by her bodyguard and eventual love interest, Soshi Miketsukami. The anime spun a tale of yearning that leaned into a low-fantasy world with the introduction of supernatural residents that live in the same apartment complex as Ririchiyo, as well as Soshi pining for the lead protagonist in such a devoted manner that it stretches beyond multiple timelines.

The new commemorative anime art piece features the core cast of Inu x Boku SS , with every Maison de Ayakashi resident accompanied by their respective bodyguards. With Ririchiyo and Soshi being the main centerpiece of the graphic, the visual also features Nobara Yukinokouji, Renshou Sorinozuka, Banri Watanuki, Zange Natsume, Karuta Roromiya and Kagerou Shoukiin, each holding party poppers, presents, and other party decorations while dressed in formal attire.

This isn't where the anniversary celebration for the series ends, though, with the official website for the anime announcing that Inu x Boku SS will continue the celebration with a special re-broadcast of the series beginning in January 2027. Leading up to the re-broadcast, there will be a special stage event in Japan as part of the Kitakyushu Pop Culture Festival featuring two of the main cast members from the series: Rina Hidaka, who plays the main protagonist Ririchiyo Shirakiin, and Yoko Hikasa who plays Nobara Yukinokouji.

Based on the original manga by the late Cocoa Fujiwara, Inu x Boku SS was an adorably unique romance anime that came out of the 2010's era that captivated fans the moment it began airing. As of writing, Inu x Boku SS has over 5.1-million copies in circulation, which skyrocketed after the anime was initially being produced and steadily climbed after the series reached its end. Even later into the series' publication, Volume 9 of Inu x Boku SS took the top slot in Oricon's sales charts in its first week on bookstore shelves with over 200,000 copies being sold. Despite the manga's success and the anime being beloved by fans, there's a vocal corner of the fanbase that's hoping the anime will someday continue.

David Production's anime adaptation only ran for a brisk 12-episodes, adapting only the first four volumes of the 11-volume series, which ultimately left out many of the darker plot twists found in the original work. Whether in spite of or because of fans' hopes that the anime will someday continue, Inu x Boku SS has maintained an active fanbase in Japan and overseas.

The franchise continues to host pop-up shops that feature new merchandise with the main cast and a variety of merchandise collaborations, including brand-new Nendoroid figures being planned by Goodsmile Company and exclusive 15th Anniversary merchandise being planned for fans of the anime in Japan. But can you believe it's been 15 years of Inu x Boku SS ? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Rachael Leigh Cook Plays Twins In Her New Hallmark Movie. I’m Surprised At What Weirded Her Out

Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas lineup this year has been one of the best yet. From reinventing the time-loop wheel to an incredible third season of Mistletoe Murders , it’s been hit after hit, and it doesn't seem to be slowing down. In fact, Thanksgiving week is going to be even bigger with the release of Lacey Chabert’s Disney World movie and Rachael Leigh Cook’s newest film, where she pulls double duty playing twins. I'm excited to see Cook take on the roles, but I'm also surprised over a concern she had.

The She’s All That star is set to play identical twins Abigail and Charlie, who end up in Wales for Christmas to help run an AirBnb/bookshop for the week. While there, both women connect with local men: Tom (Owain Yeoman), a barista who works next to the shop, and Lord Rhys (Stephan Hagan), the son of the author behind a popular book series that takes place in the town.

Differentiating between Abigail and Charlie brought up its own set of complications for Cook, as her characters are identical twins with similar preferences when it comes to their appearance. This is definitely something that hasn’t been done before, since most movies that feature twins give each character something unique to help audiences tell the difference. Thankfully, Cook found other ways to help audiences tell her characters apart — at least she hopes she did:

Hallmark movies aren’t known for their confusing nature, so I’m feeling confident about the direction of the film. If anything, it might feel like an immersive experience if viewers can’t tell her characters apart and could allow them to empathize with the men who are falling for Cook's respective characters.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Who'd win in a fight, Batman or Superman ? The truth is that if both of them decided to take each other out at a moment's notice, Batman would be laid out before he could even say "Vengeance". As much as that disappoints the Batman fan in me, it's the likely scenario given their power scales. However, we can all agree that Batman is unbeatable with prep time. We've seen this plenty of times, like in the JLA: Tower of Babel series, but Batman: The Dark Knight Returns gave us the best version of it. You can now own the original artwork of Frank Miller's classic for a cool $400,000 at Heritage Auctions .

While Batman fighting (and defeating) Superman is the highlight of the story, this particular page showcases The Dark Knight taking on the mutants that plague Gotham and their terrifying leader. The stunning page and panel work shows an old and grizzled Batman in his tank, dispersing the mutants, with the leader square in his sights. He finds himself in a dilemma, whether to take him out with one shot and break his long-standing no killing rule, or to fight him face to face at the risk of getting himself killed. The Mutant Leader is big, strong, and in his prime, and even Batman admits that he could easily be killed. However, The Dark Knight is nothing if not stubborn, even in his old age, choosing to fight him with fists rather than easily take him out with just one shot from his Bat-Tank. Unfortunately, things don't go his way.

Besides the narrative, dialogue, and artwork, what stands out about this page is the paneling. Miller and Klaus Janson lay out the scene brilliantly, with a perspective shot of Batman in his tank, surrounded by its many controls. The controls also line up to resemble the Gotham skyline, with Batman square in the middle, as if to signify his legacy in the city over the years. A mix or circular and rectangular panels follow, depicting his dilemma while also showcasing the Mutant Leader's sheer physical superiority over the hero, who is clearly past his prime. The dark ink tones further add weight to the moment, as it's a decisive moment in the narrative, which will go on to set a precedent for the rest of the story.

I won't be alone in saying that The Dark Knight Returns is up there with The Killing Joke , Year One , and The Long Halloween as one of the best ever Batman stories. It shows that he is still capable of being Gotham's savior, despite his old age and deteriorating physical prowess. While this fight doesn't go his way, he uses his superior intellect to learn from it for the rematch, where he proceeds to slice open the Mutant Leader like a surgeon on an operating table. It shows us that even in defeat, Batman always comes back stronger. This original artwork from one of Batman's best stories is well worth every dollar of that $400,000, and would make for a great addition to any fan's collection.

Which is your favorite ever Batman arc? Let us know in the comments.

And while its sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero, didn't quite achieve that same level of praise, it's still up there as not only an incredible […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Takashi Yamazaki has left an indelible mark on the film landscape with his Godzilla films . Godzilla Minus One is currently lauded as one of the greatest kaiju films of all time. And while its sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero , didn't quite achieve that same level of praise, i t's still up there as not only an incredible monster movie , but one of the best representations of post-war society—and now Minus Zero is getting an era-appropriate release on December 11th, coming back into theaters in black and white, the same way that Minus One did during its U.S. theatrical run.

In 2024, Godzilla Minus One became Godzilla Minus Color , a limited-run theatrical release in black and white that frames the film as it would have looked had it premiered in the era that inspired it. Fans absolutely loved it, and so did Yamazaki. Speaking at a press conference, the writer, director, and special effects supervisor said, “I was very happy that the North American audience embraced Godzilla Minus One and gave us positive feedback such as ‘it was incredible!’, ‘it was scary!’, and ‘it made me cry!’ And now I am very pleased to be able to release a black-and-white version for North America as well."

The general consensus is, "shut up and take my money." One fan on X said, "Wow, would you look at that. Another reason for me to watch this movie once again!! Isn't life great!" Another threw Christopher Nolan and Marvel under the bus, saying , "This and Project Hail Mary are the only movies that deserve to be rereleased. Odyssey , hell naw. Spider-Man is just a cash grab." And while some publications imply that Minus Zero has been pulled from theaters due to low viewership, it makes more sense that it's because it's already slated for a rerelease in a different format.

The black-and-white re-release is also a chance for the film's critics' and audience scores to keep climbing. While Minus One sits at 99% with critics and 98% with audiences, Minus Zero only holds 90% and 95%, respectively. Those scores are nothing to turn your nose up, but they're certainly a few points away from being as iconic as they could be. Critic Manuel São Bento sums it up best with his B+ rating, saying, "This is a sequel that respects its characters, stages monster fights that are a blast to watch, and keeps the heart of the first flick beating, even if a little softer."

And despite the logline claiming that "there is no third time. Everything ends here," it seems that might not be the case, and fans might be in for a third entry in the franchise . While Yamazaki has already started on his next movie, his first English-language film, Grandgear , he's also said that if he came back for a third installment, he'd love to bring an original kaiju to the table. “If it were up to me, I think it would be very interesting to perhaps even create an original kaiju to explore in another film," he stated.

Though his career has spanned over four decades, John Turturro still feels like it's just the beginning.

"They taught me that a job well done defines who you are. Building a house, making a dress was done brick by brick, stitch by stitch."

He called filmmaking the "magic and beauty of life" and "an offering that you hope others will receive with open hearts."

"A great writer, Cesare Pavese, once said that the only great thing in life is to begin. And I still consider myself a beginner in many ways," he concluded. "For me, when I do a job, every job is like a first love. And I consider this award an encouragement to continue to try."

articles.title: The X-Men Became Marvel Legends by Borrowing a Winning Formula From DC, Just Not the One You Think
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics The X-Men are basically the once and future king of Marvel. The team is finally about to make its full MCU debut after years of teases, first appearing as a team in Avengers: Doomsday (and perhaps Avengers: Secret Wars, but most fans assume the FoX-Men are about to die in the earlier movie) before an […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The X-Men are basically the once and future king of Marvel. The team is finally about to make its full MCU debut after years of teases, first appearing as a team in Avengers: Doomsday (and perhaps Avengers: Secret Wars , but most fans assume the FoX-Men are about to die in the earlier movie) before an all-new cast of mutants takes their place on the big screen in 2028. Marvel now has the power of Disney behind them; the X-Men are going to be everywhere in the years to come. The MCU has fallen from grace, but I think we all know just how massive the men and women of X are going to be in the years to come.

This isn't the first time that the X-Men are positioned to become the most popular team in comics. The team was the biggest superhero team of the '80s and '90s, with the rise of the Avengers in the '00s finally seeing the X-Men take a back seat to another team. Books like Uncanny X-Men , X-Men , and Wolverine sold in the six figure range for years, with Uncanny and X-Men holding the top spots of the sales charts for nearly every month of the '80s and '90s. Their rise in the mid '70s came during a Marvel boom period, where the House of Ideas was proving that that successes of the Silver Age weren't a fluke. Those issues of X-Men went in a new direction with their new team, with the X-Men becoming the greatest superhero soap opera of all time. However, they weren't the first superhero soap opera; that was the Legion of Superheroes . The X-Men stole the Legion approach and that's the only reason they've reached the level of popularity they have.

So, to begin with, we need to define what I mean when I say "superhero soap opera". Basically, this approach to superheroes is all about how much the stories revolve around the personal lives of the characters. All superhero books get into that sort of thing, but the true superhero soap opera books are all about it. You have a bunch of beautiful, damaged people together; the shenanigans of their life are going to be entertaining.

The Legion of Superheroes were one of the first practitioners of this art. The Legion has a massive membership , the team consisting of alien teens from across the 31st century. Half of the fun of the Legion is the web of relationships and the way they all react to each other. There are cliques within the team and the various members all have their own supporting characters and enemies. While Legion comics gave readers pulse-pounding superhero action, it also gave readers the kind of soap opera stories that hooked them.

The Legion are integral to the history of DC , but in recent years have fallen from grace, their stories much too complicated. One of the things about jumping into the various Legion reboots is that all of them play off of one another. Knowing the relationships and the team members' histories makes it easier to get into them. They are the most daunting team to get into in comics. Sure, the superhero soap opera basics are always fun, but without knowing the history, it doesn't always hit the same.

The Silver Age X-Men were a lot like the Legion; they were both teen teams, for example. However, the difference is the X-Men's civil rights connections, something that was played up in the early months of their adventures, as they battled both evil mutants and human bigots. However, the team never really caught on. Fans just didn't really care about them as characters, which was rare for Marvel in the Silver Age. By contrast, the Legion focused on its characters and their lives and fans loved it. The X-Men had cool villains, great costumes, and entertaining powers, but they didn't have good characters, which led to them almost going the way of the dodo.

Giant-Size X-Men #1 is where the major Legion similarities began. It was drawn by Dave Cockrum, who had pitched Legion characters to DC. He modified those designs for the X-Men and would base the Imperial Guard on the Legion. However, it was more than just the looks and powers that the X-Men would take from the Legion. Chris Claremont came aboard the X-Men and he knew what had to be done: focus on the characters.

There are lots of things you can point at as the reason for the X-Men's success, but one of the most important is how great the characters were. The X-Men felt like fully-realized characters compared to other Marvel books of the day. Go back and read those old X-Men comics and you'll be instantly drawn into the lives of the characters. Uncanny X-Men had amazing superhero stories, sure. Classics like the M'Kraan Crystal saga, "The Dark Phoenix Saga", "Days of Future Past", the Brood Saga, "Lifedeath", "The Trial of Magneto", and many more are all era-defining stories. However, what makes them so great is the quiet moments, the way they built their characters, how the events affected them.

Much like the Legion, a truly massive group of X-Men became the focus of the book during its most popular years. There was a web of relationships between all of the characters and little cliques within the greater group. If you don't know their histories, you can still enjoy them, but gain a greater appreciation once you know the past. One of the games that comic fans like to play is comparing who is who in the various universes. So, for example, saying the Avengers are the Marvel Justice League. The X-Men are Marvel's Legion, their success built in the same way.

The Legion cultivated a devoted fandom over the years thanks to the character. Fans learned to love them and wanted to spend more time in their lives. Others found them complex, but their fans gloried in taking ten minutes to describe the history of Starboy to a confused friend asking them for help. Their books were superhero soap operas and their approach was the one that Chris Claremont used to make the team popular again.

The X-Men became popular in the '70s and '80s not just because they were in cool fights with their enemies but because of who the team were. None of their stories would work so well if Claremont and company hadn't built up the characters and their lives, though. It's the exact same thing that years of Legion creators had done over the years, building the characters, making us love to spend time in their lives. The Legion made the superhero soap opera popular, but the X-Men perfected it.

Do you think that X-Men are Marvel's Legion of Superheroes? Do you think they copied the Legion approach or am I completely wrong? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.content:
Todd Boehly gave an insight into his no nonsense approach to investing in sports and entertainment in the concluding fireside chat of the Qatar Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days over the weekend.

The billionaire investor's holding company Eldridge holds some $75B in assets including stakes in Backrooms distributor A24, and Fulwell Entertainment as well as the Los Angeles Lakers, the Los Angeles Sparks, the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Trent Rockets among many more.

The holding is also a partner with Deadline owner Penske Media in the Penske Media Eldridge unit encompassing live TV entertainment specialist Dick Clark Productions as well as events such as the Golden Globes and SXSW. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Joe Russo Talks 'Doomsday' Teaser-Trailer Strategy Ahead Of Rumored Monday Drop: "I Have To interact With Fans" News Watermelon Expands Production Ambitions As It Seals Partnership With Qatar's Film Committee

Boehly first connected with A24 cofounder Daniel Katz, when the latter headed Guggenheim Partners' film finance group in New York, while he was president of the global investment firm before leaving to create Eldridge. Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

“One of the things I believe is that there's very few entertainment people that understand math… the math of entertainment is really about understanding how are you taking risk and then how are you distributing risk,” he said in the chat entitled “Playing to Win".

“It's no different than any other industry, if you're thinking about what amount of risk you are willing to take and then how are you going to feed that risk,” he added.

Boehly said Katz had impressed him from the start for his ability to identify and work with risk during his time with Guggenheim Partners.

“Daniel's real magic, when he worked on our trading floor from, let's call it like 2008 to 2012, he didn't take a lot of risks, but he said ‘no’ a lot,” he said.

“There was a slate that was done by a group called Stark Investments, and one of their big films was Poseidon . I remember it showed up on our desk. And Daniel was immediately like, this is a disaster. It's going to cost so much money, you know, they're not going to be able to make any return on it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The $160M disaster movie by Wolfgang Petersen went down in film financing folklore after it faltered at the box office and failed to gross enough to cover its P&A costs.

Boehly provided $19M in seed money for A24 as Katz launched the company in 2012 with David Fenkel and Joh Hodges. It was last publicly valued at $3.5 billion in June 2024.

“Everyone told me in Hollywood that there's no room for another distribution company,” recalled the businessman. “His early successes with Spring Breakers and The Bling Ring were really structured finance trades.”

“You're not really allowed to talk about that in the entertainment world because everything's creative and creator driven… what Daniel was really good at, because he sat on a trading desk and he understood risk and he understood math, he was really good at figuring out how am I going to get my money back using different windows.”

Starring James Franco, Selena Gomez, Vanessa Hudgens, Harmony Korine’s Spring Breakers premiered in competition in Venice and went on to gross $31M.

“Spring Breakers cost a couple million bucks to buy, and he ended up making 10 million bucks or so very quickly on, because he really understood that it's a structured finance straight," said Boehly.

He added that beyond Katz's business savviness, the company had also understood how to tap into social media to generate audience engagement as well as how to plug into trends of the moment.

“One of the things that A24 has done an amazing job at is being able to read the cultural zeitgeist. I think Civil War was really well timed; Marty Supreme was very well timed with Timothée Chalamet and his ascension as probably one of the top actors for the next couple of decades."

Boehly also highlighted A24’s strategy of growing a cohort of directors and actors, who returned to work with the company on a regular basis.

“He wants repeat customers. He wants the directors coming back… he wants the actors coming back… because then it's not a transaction, it becomes a recurring business with enterprise," said Boehly.

"So many people think about the film business, ‘Oh, it’s a transaction’. But if you're really thinking about how to build an enterprise, then you need to make sure that you have a recurring revenue base. And the way you do that in this industry is you get repeat users."

He also gave insight into how Katz constructs A24's slate in a way that enables it to work with established names and newcomers and turn a profit, suggesting that over a portfolio of 15 films, nine would be "the core bread and butter".

"It's a budget of 25 to 40 million bucks. It's the expectation that he's going to make 1.35 times,” he explained. “And if you think about the math of it again, you get 0.8 times your money back right away or very quickly. So, when you think about the risk that you have, you're in for 0.2. If you make 1.35 and your risk capital is 0.2, but you're going to make six, seven times that 0.2.”

“And then he'll take three big swings and make something that has the capacity to become multiple films out of the content… he'll take 1.2 times. So, he'll modify his expectations on the rate of return to achieve something that might have more enterprise value or longevity on the back of it.”

Boehly suggested the final three films would be by up-and-coming young directors, and would require time, energy and effort rather than big financial investments and risk. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

“He's always thinking about how do I build that portfolio in order to have my bread and butter, have the opportunity to have something that's got longevity and then find someone who's going to be special in the industry,” he said.

articles.title: Guarding Stars Was Adorable, But Can We Talk About That Stalker Twist?
articles.summary: There was some soggy fruitcake amidst this Christmasy feast.
articles.content:
This year’s Christmas movie releases are in full swing now that it’s mid-November, and I knew I had to check out Guarding Stars with my Netflix subscription . I mean, it unites Gilmore Girls ’ Jared Padalecki with Gossip Girl ’s Leighton Meester , so I was in for the 2000s nostalgia alone. I was really digging this lighthearted rom-com (that’s sometimes an action movie), but then that twist just made me go “WTF!” Let’s talk about it. But be warned, there are SPOILERS ahead!

Before we get into my lows about Guarding Stars , I have to give the movie its flowers. I’ve seen a lot of holiday rom-coms, and this one had the right amount of sweetness and depth I want from this kind of movie. It follows the fake dating trope pretty much to a T, but I really enjoyed what Padalecki and Meester in particular brought to it as Jack and Hannah.

It’s the kind of movie where we all know they were going to fall in love by the end, but I was instantly curious about how these two were going to fall for each other. I like that they brought out the softness in each other despite both of them being otherwise hardened by their current lives, and I really liked the mother/son dynamic between Jack and Andie Macdowell’s Connie.

However, I thought the Guarding Stars really dropped the ball on the whole “stalker” plotline. Not that I’d expect it to be a huge part of the movie to begin with, but when it was revealed that Nadine was Jack’s stalker near the end, I was so taken aback. It felt way too convenient that one of two people he meets outside of his family and his bodyguard crew ended up being the stalker, and particularly having happened to be in the same place where he was hiding away.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One Piece 's latest chapter has begun unraveling a mystery that the series introduced over three years ago, in May 2023, and it could change much of what fans know about the series. Given that One Piece is currently in its final saga, it was evident that the series would begin unveiling the mysteries it has built up over more than 1,000 chapters. While several have been explained here and there, one of the most intriguing mysteries the series has kept concealed revolves around the Void Century. There are hundreds of speculations about what this century holds, but a few characters have been particularly connected to it.

Among the several characters tied to the Void Century , one of the most intriguing is Nefertari D. Lili, the queen of Alabasta during that era. She was one of the founding royals behind the World Government; however, she refused to become a Celestial Dragon and instead returned to her country. This has been unveiled and hinted at several times in the past, ever since King Cobra first mentioned the queen and revealed that she had also left behind a letter. The latest chapter hints that Robin may finally read this very letter, and it couldn't have been unveiled at a more perfect time.

One Piece Chapter 1195 had subtly revealed that a woman named Lili once lived in Elbaph, and now the latest chapter, 1199, unveils that what she left behind was a letter that Robin is about to read. It is now evident that this is indeed the same letter Cobra mentioned, potentially containing an important piece of information related to the Void Century. However, the timing of this revelation is also intriguing, as Luffy has mysteriously transformed into a rogue version of his Gear 5 appearance , displaying entirely monkey-like behavior and features. Perhaps the letter Robin is about to read could have something to do with this transformation.

It has been speculated that Lili was at the center of the conflict involving Imu and Joyboy, with some fans even suggesting a possible love triangle. That may very well be true, and Joyboy, as Nika, could also be connected to the form Luffy has now transformed into. One Piece still has a lot to explain about Luffy's new appearance, and with speculation already suggesting that this is a second version of the Sun God , feared as the destroyer of the world, the series has plenty of questions to answer. The Elbaph mural also hints at this very version. With the mention of Lili and a letter that is finally about to be read, the series has raised the stakes surrounding this mystery and the answers it is about to unveil.

The Void Century remains one of the most intriguing mysteries One Piece has concealed, and even a single piece of information about it could help connect the dots and reveal what actually happened during this period. By bringing Lili's letter into the picture alongside Luffy's mysterious new appearance, One Piece is in the perfect position to finally unveil some of its biggest secrets. Honestly, the series couldn't be better prepared to address these mysteries, and it should begin doing so in the next chapter without delaying any further.

As John Madden 's life gets the biopic treatment, his longtime colleague and friend Al Davis ' family is not pleased with their late patriarch's portrayal.

Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis , whose father Al recruited Madden to coach for the NFL team when they were located in Oakland in 1967, criticized David O. Russell 's Madden for its "totally unfair" depiction his father (portrayed by Christian Bale ), who died at age 82 in 2011.

"It was full of turducken," he told USA Today of the movie, referencing the Thanksgiving dish Madden popularized.

Mark continued, "As far as representations of my dad, yeah, that hurts, and I did the best I could to protect him. It's absolutely a crime that they're able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there's nobody around to protect their legacies. It's just unfair. I don't know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }
